items.text: It's so noisy right now. Everyone shouting and making a lot of noise in the halls.
items.why: right now → is shouting. The verb be is missing.
items.fix: It's so noisy right now. Everyone is shouting and making a lot of noise in the halls.

items.text: I haven't been in this town very long. I just get here two weeks ago.
items.why: two weeks ago → simple past: got.
items.fix: I haven't been in this town very long. I just got here two weeks ago.

items.text: I'm really glad you to come to my hometown next year.
items.why: next year → are going to come / will come.
items.fix: I'm really glad you are going to come to my hometown next year.

items.text: Why were you deciding to become a nurse?
items.why: One finished decision → Why did you decide.
items.fix: Why did you decide to become a nurse?

items.text: I am in Australia for the last four months. During this time, I had done many things and saw many places.
items.why: Up to now → have been, have done, (have) seen.
items.fix: I have been in Australia for the last four months. During this time, I have done many things and seen many places.

items.text: By the time I graduate from college, I will have taken out several student loans.
items.why: Before a future time → will have taken.

items.title: First find the time
lines: Every sentence has a time clue.
The clue picks the tense.

items.title: Clue words
lines: Tap the clues. Each one calls a tense.

items.text: Her classes ___ at 6:00 every evening.
items.why: every evening = a habit → simple present.

items.title: Finished, or in progress?

examples.text: Yesterday I called her at 6:30.
She was attending class at that time.

items.tip: A long action in the middle + a short event = was -ing + simple past.

items.text: I called at 6:30, but she didn't answer because she ___ class at that time.
items.why: In progress at 6:30 → was attending.

items.title: How long? Add have / had
lines: Up to now → has been -ing.
Up to a past moment → had been -ing.

examples.text: She has been sleeping for an hour.
She had been sleeping for 15 minutes by the time I got there.

lines: Find the time clue first. It picks the tense.
How long? up to now → has been -ing. Up to then → had been -ing.

examples.text: Her classes begin at 6:00 every evening.
She was attending class at that time.
She has been sleeping for an hour.

items.text: Malia is in my evening speech class. She ___ speech this semester.
items.why: this semester = around now → is studying.

items.text: She ___ some other night classes.
items.why: also goes after is.

items.text: Her classes ___ at 6:00 every evening.
items.why: every evening = a habit → simple present.

items.text: Yesterday Malia woke up at 5:00 A.M. She ___ when her alarm clock rang.
items.why: Before the alarm rang → had already gotten up.

items.text: She had already gotten up when her alarm clock ___.
items.why: The later past event → simple past: rang.

items.text: Malia ___ at the mall during the day.
items.why: Her regular job → simple present.

items.text: She ___ a big breakfast before she leaves.
items.why: always + simple present.

items.text: She always eats a big breakfast before she ___.
items.why: A habit → simple present.

items.text: She ___ time for a lunch break.
items.why: A habit, negative → doesn't usually have.

items.text: Malia is in class every evening from 6:00 to 9:00. Yesterday I ___ her at 6:30.
items.why: Yesterday, one event → simple past.

items.text: But she ___.
items.why: Yesterday, negative → didn't answer.

items.text: She didn't answer because she ___ class at that time.
items.why: In progress at 6:30 → was attending.

items.text: I can't call her tomorrow night because she ___ class then.
items.why: In progress at a future time → will be attending.

items.text: She took a nap from 10:00 to 10:30. I arrived at 10:15. When I ___ there, Malia was sleeping.
items.why: A finished past event → got.

items.text: When I got there at 10:15, Malia ___.
items.why: In progress when I arrived → was sleeping.

items.text: She ___ for 15 minutes by the time I got there.
items.why: How long before a past moment → had been sleeping.

items.text: Right now Malia ___.
items.why: Right now → is sleeping.

items.text: She ___ asleep an hour ago.
items.why: an hour ago → simple past: fell.

items.text: She ___ for an hour.
items.why: How long up to now → has been sleeping.
items.ctx: She fell asleep an hour ago. She is still asleep.

items.text: Tomorrow is her first day off. After she ___ dinner, Malia is going to meet me.
items.why: After after (future) → present, not will.

items.text: After she has dinner, Malia ___ me and a friend.
items.why: The main part → future.

items.text: In other words, she ___ dinner by the time she meets us.
items.why: Finished before a future time → will have had.

items.text: She will have had dinner by the time she ___ us.
items.why: After by the time (future) → simple present.

talk.title: Now, yesterday, tonight
talk.task: Claude asks about right now, yesterday at this time, and tonight at midnight.
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English speaking partner. I am reviewing all the verb tenses. Ask me these questions one at a time and wait for my answer: What are you doing right now? How long have you been doing that? What were you doing at this time yesterday? What did you do after that? What will you be doing tonight at midnight? What places have you visited in your life, and when did you visit one of them? I answer in complete sentences. Check that my tense matches the tense of your question.

items.title: Stories walk in the simple past
lines: One event after another → simple past.
chips: I put it in the lock.

items.title: Step back with had
lines: Something happened even earlier? Use had + part 3.

examples.text: I felt very stupid about what I had done.

items.text: I felt very stupid about what I ___.
items.why: It happened before “felt” → had done.

items.title: Finished or up to now?

examples.text: Three weeks ago, Vanessa started the book.
She hasn't finished it yet.
She has read many famous novels.

items.tip: ago, yesterday → simple past. yet, in her lifetime, since → present perfect.

items.text: Since the beginning of the summer, Vanessa ___ three other books.
items.why: Since … up to now → has finished.

lines: A story: events in the simple past. Earlier events: had + part 3.
Up to now (yet, since, so far, just) → present perfect.

examples.text: I felt very stupid about what I had done.
She hasn't finished it yet.

items.text: When I ___ home to my apartment last night, I took out my key.
items.why: last night → simple past.

items.text: I ___ out my key to open the door as usual.
items.why: take, took, taken.

items.text: As always, I ___ it in the lock.
items.why: put, put, put.

items.text: But the door ___.
items.why: Past, negative → didn't open.

items.text: I ___ my key again and again with no luck.
items.why: try → tried.

items.text: So I ___ on the door for my wife to let me in.
items.why: Regular: knocked.

items.text: Finally the door ___.
items.why: The next event → simple past.

items.text: But I ___ my wife on the other side.
items.why: Past, negative → didn't see.

items.text: I ___ a stranger.
items.why: see, saw, seen.

items.text: I ___ to get into the wrong apartment!
items.why: All that time before the door opened → had been trying.

items.text: I quickly ___.
items.why: The next event → simple past.

items.text: And I ___ to my own apartment.
items.why: go, went, gone.

items.text: I ___ very stupid.
items.why: feel, felt, felt.

items.text: I felt very stupid about what I ___.
items.why: Before “felt” → had done.

items.text: The man broke the lock on the door.
items.why: The key just didn't work. Wrong door!

items.text: The man saw a stranger in the apartment.
items.why: A stranger opened the door.

items.text: The man's wife opened the door.
items.why: A stranger opened it, not his wife.

items.text: The man felt he had done something stupid.
items.why: He felt very stupid about it.

items.text: Tom has had a busy day so far. He ___ the floor.
items.why: What has he been doing? → has been + -ing.
items.ctx: Right now Tom is taking a break. What has he been doing?

items.text: He ___ dinner.
items.why: An activity up to now → has been cooking.

items.text: Yesterday Tom ___ the car.
items.why: Yesterday → simple past.

items.text: Yesterday he ___ some flowers.
items.why: Yesterday → simple past.

items.text: Look! Tom ___ the bike. It works again.
items.why: just + result now → has just fixed.

items.text: Tom was tired last night because he ___ English words all day.
items.why: How long before a past moment → had been memorizing.

items.text: Three weeks ago, Vanessa ___ to read War and Peace.
items.why: Three weeks ago → simple past.

items.text: She ___ it because her literature teacher recommended it.
items.why: She is in the middle of it now → is reading.

items.text: It is a very long novel, and it ___ many characters.
items.why: A fact; have = state verb → has.

items.text: She ___ reading it yet.
items.why: not … yet → hasn't finished.

items.text: Since the beginning of the summer, Vanessa ___ three other books.
items.why: Since … up to now → has finished.

items.text: In her lifetime, she ___ many famous novels.
items.why: In her life up to now → has read.

items.text: This is the first Tolstoy novel she ___.
items.why: the first … she has ever read.

items.text: After she finishes this book, she ___ another Tolstoy novel.
items.why: Her next plan → future.

talk.title: What has Tom been doing?
talk.task: Imagine a busy day. Tell Claude what you have been doing, then say it again with yesterday and with just.
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English writing partner. I am reviewing present perfect progressive, simple past and present perfect. Ask me to imagine a busy day at home and write four sentences about what I have been doing (present perfect progressive), using verbs like cook, fix, vacuum, memorize, plant, wash. Then ask me to rewrite them with 'yesterday' (simple past), and then with 'just' (present perfect). Check each tense.

talk.title: Make up a story
talk.task: Scene: a kitchen full of smoke, a dog with a cake, a surprised family at the door. Tell what happened.
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English speaking partner. Describe this scene to me and ask me to invent the story: a family opens their front door and finds the kitchen full of smoke, the dog eating a birthday cake, and water on the floor. Ask me one question at a time: What had happened before they came home? What was the dog doing when they opened the door? What did they do next? What are they going to do now? Check my verb tenses.

talk.title: About this course
talk.task: Claude asks about your studies: what you have studied, will have studied, and are going to do.
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English speaking partner. Ask me these questions one at a time: What have you been studying lately? What is one tense you have studied, and when did you study it? What will you have studied by the end of this month? Had you studied verb tenses before this year? Where are you going to be living next year? What has happened in the news recently? I answer in complete sentences. Check that my tense matches your question.

lesson.title: Learn: helper verbs tell the tense

items.title: Look at the next word
lines: The helper verb matches the word after it.

items.title: have or had?
lines: Now is the end point → have / has.
A past moment is the end point → had.

examples.text: Billy has never seen snow before.
I had never been in such hot weather before that trip.

items.text: It ___ been raining sideways all morning. When will it stop?
items.why: Up to now + been → has.

items.title: State verbs stay simple
lines: like, want, know, believe: no -ing.
chips: ❌ I am believing he is right.
✅ We want to see it again.
❌ We are wanting to see it again.

items.text: I don't like my job. I ___ my brother is right.
items.why: believe is a state verb. No -ing.

lines: -ing after is / was / been. Past participle after has / have / had.
Now is the end point → have. A past moment is the end point → had.

examples.text: Billy has never seen snow before.
I had never been in such hot weather before.

items.text: When I was in my country…
options: When I was in my country, I want to come to Canada for my studies.
When I was in my country, I wanted to come to Canada for my studies.
When I was in my country, I have wanted to come to Canada for my studies.
items.why: When I was … = finished time → wanted.

items.text: I had cousins in Canada, so…
options: I wasn't nervous because I had cousins in Canada.
I didn't be nervous because I had cousins in Canada.
I not nervous because I had cousins in Canada.
items.why: be in the past, negative → wasn't.

items.text: Three months, and I'm still here.
options: I had been here for three months and I like it.
I have been here for three months and I like it.
I am here for three months and I like it.
items.why: Up to now → have been.

items.text: My plan for the year
options: I study here for a year.
I will studying here for a year.
I am going to study here for a year.
items.why: A plan → am going to + study.

items.text: When I go home…
options: When I return to my country, I will have been away for 15 months.
When I return to my country, I am going to be away for 15 months.
When I return to my country, I was away for 15 months.
items.why: How long by a future time → will have been.

items.text: It ___ snowing again.
items.why: Now + -ing, it → is.

items.text: It is snowing again. The roads ___ be slippery.
items.why: A prediction + be → will.

items.text: Billy ___ never seen snow before. He likes trying to catch the flakes.
items.why: In his life up to now, he → has.

items.text: It ___ been raining sideways all morning. When will it stop?
items.why: Up to now + been raining → has.

items.text: Shhh! I ___ trying to listen to the forecast.
items.why: Right now, I → am.

items.text: It sounds like a heat advisory ___ be in effect later this week.
items.why: later this week + be → will.

items.text: When we ___ visiting my in-laws in India last month, there was a heat wave.
items.why: In progress in the past, we → were.

items.text: It was like an oven. I ___ never been in such hot weather before.
items.why: Before that past time → had.

items.text: The lack of rain this month ___ made the smog really bad.
items.why: Result now, it → has.

items.text: My eyes ___ been watering since I got here.
items.why: since … up to now, eyes = they → have.

items.text: When I ___ driving on the freeway, freezing rain had just started to fall.
items.why: In progress in the past, I → was.

items.text: When I was driving on the freeway, freezing rain ___ just started to fall. It was scary.
items.why: Just before that past moment → had.

items.text: It ___ been a colder than normal winter. I'm ready for spring.
items.why: Up to now, it → has.

items.text: I ___ never experienced such violent weather until I came here.
items.why: until I came (past) → had.

items.text: Since last January
options: I am studying here since last January.
I was studying here since last January.
I have been studying here since last January.
items.why: since … up to now → have been studying.

items.text: Hassan went home.
options: By the time Hassan returned to his country, he had been away from home for more than three years.
By the time Hassan returned to his country, he has been away from home for more than three years.
By the time Hassan returned to his country, he is away from home for more than three years.
items.why: Before a past time → had been.

items.text: Neil's plan
options: After Neil will graduate, he is going to return to his hometown.
After Neil graduate, he going to return to his hometown.
After Neil graduates, he is going to return to his hometown.
items.why: After after → graduates. Main part: is going to.

items.text: Still single
options: I want to get married, but I don't meet the right person yet.
I want to get married, but I haven't met the right person yet.
I want to get married, but I hadn't met the right person yet.
items.why: not … yet, up to now → haven't met.

items.text: A great movie
options: We have been seeing that movie twice, and now we want to see it again.
We have seen that movie twice, and now we are wanting to see it again.
We have seen that movie twice, and now we want to see it again.
items.why: twice → have seen. want = state verb.

items.text: My job
options: I don't like my job. My brother wants me to quit. I believe he is right.
I am not like my job. My brother wants me to quit. I am believing he is right.
I don't like my job. My brother want me to quit. I believed he is right.
items.why: like, want, believe: state verbs, simple present.

items.text: After dinner
options: We cleaned up the kitchen after our dinner guests were leaving.
We cleaned up the kitchen after our dinner guests are going to leave.
We cleaned up the kitchen after our dinner guests left.
items.why: A past story: after + simple past.

items.text: My neighbors
options: I know my neighbors Mr. and Mrs. Sanchez ever since I was a child.
I have known my neighbors Mr. and Mrs. Sanchez ever since I was a child.
I knew my neighbors Mr. and Mrs. Sanchez ever since I have been a child.
items.why: ever since … up to now → have known.

items.text: An earthquake
options: Many scientists believe there will be a major earthquake in California in the near future.
Many scientists believe there going to be a major earthquake in California in the near future.
Many scientists believe there will to be a major earthquake in California in the near future.
items.why: will + be. No to.

items.text: The common cold
options: By the end of the 21st century, man will had discovered the cure for the common cold.
By the end of the 21st century, man will have discovered the cure for the common cold.
By the end of the 21st century, man will discovered the cure for the common cold.
items.why: By a future time → will have discovered.

options: Now the passengers are waiting in the baggage claim area.
After the plane lands, the passengers will be waiting in the baggage claim area.
items.why: has just landed = it is on the ground now.

items.say: Bill has been lying on the beach all afternoon.
items.why: has been lying = still there now.

items.say: It's been raining for three days.
items.why: It's been raining = it is still raining.

items.say: The movie had already started when we got to the theater.
options: People said “Shhh” as we sat down.
We missed the first half hour.
items.why: had already started = we were late.

items.say: Maya has finished her last flying lesson.
options: She's going to take another lesson.
items.why: has finished her last lesson = no more lessons.

items.say: The police have been looking for the bank robber for ten years.
items.why: have been looking = still looking now.

talk.title: The nosy reporter
talk.task: Pretend to be a famous person. Claude is a reporter asking about your past, present and future.
talk.claudePrompt: You are a friendly but nosy newspaper reporter and I am a famous living person (I will tell you my name first; I can invent answers). Interview me with one question at a time about my past (When did you ...?), my life up to now (How long have you ...? Have you ever ...?), my present (What are you working on now?) and my future (What are you going to do next year?). Check that the tense of my answer matches your question.

lesson.title: Learn: tenses in a real email

items.title: An email mixes tenses
lines: News up to now, things that happened, plans.
Each part has its own tense.

items.title: lately vs. yesterday

examples.text: I have been very busy lately.
A friend has been staying with me since last Thursday.
Yesterday we went to a park.
I got your email two weeks ago.

items.tip: Ask: is the time finished, or does it reach now?

items.text: A friend ___ with me since last Thursday.
items.why: since … up to now → has been staying.

items.title: Now and next
lines: right now → am -ing.
A timetable → simple present. After + present.

examples.text: Right now I am sitting at my desk.
My friend's plane leaves in a few hours.

items.text: I'm going to take a nap after I ___ back from the airport.
items.why: After after → simple present.

lines: lately / since / in the past two weeks → have (been) …
yesterday / ago → simple past. Right now → am -ing.

examples.text: I have been very busy lately.
Yesterday we went to a park.
Right now I am sitting at my desk.

items.text: I ___ your long email about two weeks ago.
items.why: two weeks ago → simple past.

items.text: I ___ to find time to write you back ever since.
items.why: ever since, up to now → have been trying.

items.text: I ___ very busy lately.
items.why: lately → have been.

items.text: In the past two weeks, I ___ four tests.
items.why: In the past two weeks, up to now → have had.

items.text: A friend ___ with me since last Thursday.
items.why: since … still here → has been staying.

items.text: She wanted to see the city, so we ___ a lot of time visiting interesting places.
items.why: This visit, up to now → have been spending.

items.text: We ___ to the zoo, the art museum, and the waterfront.
items.why: No time said, up to now → have been.

items.text: Yesterday we ___ to a park.
items.why: Yesterday → simple past.

items.text: And we ___ a hot-air balloon race.
items.why: Still yesterday → simple past.

items.text: Between the city and my exams, I ___ enough time to breathe.
items.why: These weeks up to now → have barely had.

items.text: Right now it ___ 3:00 A.M.
items.why: Right now, a fact → is.

items.text: And I ___ at my desk.
items.why: Right now → am sitting.

items.text: I ___ here for five hours doing my studying.
items.why: for five hours, up to now → have been sitting.

items.text: My friend's plane ___ in a few hours.
items.why: A timetable; plane = it → leaves.

items.text: So I ___ not to go to bed.
items.why: The decision is made → simple past.
items.ctx: My friend's plane leaves in a few hours.

items.text: That's why I ___ to you at such an early hour.
items.why: Right now → am writing.

items.text: I ___ a little sleepy, but I would rather stay up.
items.why: Changing right now → am getting.

items.text: I ___ a nap after I get back from the airport.
items.why: A plan → am going to take.

items.text: I am going to take a nap after I ___ back.
items.why: After after → simple present.

items.text: How ___ along?
items.why: These days → are you getting.

items.text: How ___ your classes going?
items.why: classes = they + going → are.

talk.title: Write your own email
talk.task: Write a short email to a friend: what you're doing now, did yesterday, have done lately, and will do next.
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English writing partner. Ask me to write a short email (5-7 sentences) to a friend about my life: what I am doing right now, what I do every day, what I have been doing lately, something I did at a specific time, and something I am going to do. Then check all my verbs for correct tense, show me the corrections one at a time, and tell me what I did well.

talk.title: News report
talk.task: Tell Claude about a recent news event in 4-5 sentences. Claude asks two questions.
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English speaking partner. Ask me to summarize a recent news event in 4-5 sentences. Then ask me two follow-up questions about it (one about the past, one about what will happen next). Check my verb tenses, especially simple past for finished events and present perfect for recent news with no time.

talk.title: Beat procrastination
talk.task: The Pomodoro idea: work 25 minutes, rest 5. Tell Claude about your own study habits.
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English speaking partner. The Pomodoro technique means working for 25 minutes without interruption and then taking a 5-minute break. Ask me one question at a time: Do you have problems with procrastination? What have you tried so far? Have you ever used a timer to study? Are you going to try the Pomodoro technique this week? Check my verb tenses.

items.text: In 1985, my parents [were emigrating] to the United States from Brazil.
options: In 1985, my parents have emigrated to the United States from Brazil.
In 1985, my parents emigrated to the United States from Brazil.
In 1985, my parents emigrate to the United States from Brazil.
items.why: In 1985, one finished event → emigrated.

items.text: Before that, they [have never traveled] outside of Brazil.
options: Before that, they had never traveled outside of Brazil.
Before that, they never travel outside of Brazil.
Before that, they are never traveling outside of Brazil.
items.why: Before a past time → had never traveled.

items.text: Eventually, they [settle] in California.
options: Eventually, they have settled in California.
Eventually, they are settling in California.
items.why: A finished event in the story → settled.

items.text: My twin sister and I were born ten years later and [are growing] up there.
options: My twin sister and I were born ten years later and grew up there.
My twin sister and I were born ten years later and grow up there.
My twin sister and I were born ten years later and have been growing up there.
items.why: Childhood is finished → grew up.

items.text: Last year, I [had gone] to Brazil for the first time to meet extended family.
options: Last year, I have gone to Brazil for the first time to meet extended family.
Last year, I went to Brazil for the first time to meet extended family.
Last year, I was going to Brazil for the first time to meet extended family.
items.why: Last year, one event → went.

items.text: I had always [want] to learn more about my family's background.
options: I had always wanting to learn more about my family's background.
I had always wants to learn more about my family's background.
I had always wanted to learn more about my family's background.
items.why: had + past participle: wanted.

items.text: My dreams finally [were coming] true.
options: My dreams finally have been coming true.
items.why: One finished event → came true.

items.text: It's so noisy right now. Everyone [shouting] in the halls.
options: It's so noisy right now. Everyone shouts in the halls.
It's so noisy right now. Everyone is shouting in the halls.
It's so noisy right now. Everyone shouted in the halls.
items.why: right now → is shouting.

items.text: I haven't been in this town very long. I just [get] here two weeks ago.
options: I haven't been in this town very long. I just got here two weeks ago.
I haven't been in this town very long. I have just gotten here two weeks ago.
I haven't been in this town very long. I am just getting here two weeks ago.
items.why: two weeks ago → simple past: got.

items.text: Why [were you deciding] to become a nurse?
options: Why you decided to become a nurse?
Why have you been deciding to become a nurse?
Why did you decide to become a nurse?
items.why: One finished decision → did you decide.
